title: Minimax Designs for Replicated Size-Two Split-Plot Experiments with Bounded Outcomes
banked_reason: D0.5 general referee: tier incremental, floor field, paper_score_ceiling 6.3 < 7.4, salvageable=false; mixed-interaction characterization remains open.
gap_reasons: The headline mixed-interaction characterization is still an unresolved question: the delivered positive independent-upper cost and order-width bounds supply no sign or value for Delta_W, so the current kernel is strictly weaker than the promised balance-after-whole-plot-relaxation result.

It does not establish the advertised cross-layer interaction: R_3^{FI} and R_3^{FF} are unknown, so the sign of Delta_3 and the claim that subplot balance becomes costly specifically after relaxing whole-plot balance remain unsettled.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 established the global minimax, endpoint-orbit, W=2, and W=3 independent-upper results, then derived all-design risk brackets. D0.5 math review passed, but the fixed-upper risks and mixed interaction promised by the original topic remain open; the general referee rated the honest package incremental below the field floor. A future attempt needs exact fixed-upper dual certificates or a hierarchical boundary-layer analysis, rather than a new framing of these brackets.
tldr: In replicated size-two split plots, independent fair assignment is globally minimax under common bounded potential outcomes. An explicit design-stabilizing group, endpoint quotient, and Bernstein extension reduce every unrestricted risk to a finite certified orbit game. Global design minimaxity and the exact HT benchmark sandwich all four designs as \(r_W^{\mathrm{un}}\leq R_W^{II}\leq R_W^{uv}=V_W^{uv}\leq H_W^u\). Consequently every risk is \(W^{-1}+O(W^{-4/3})\), both lower-stage costs satisfy \(|C_W^u|\leq H_W^u-r_W^{\mathrm{un}}=O(W^{-4/3})\), and \(|\Delta_W|=O(W^{-4/3})\), without a sign or sharp coefficient. The lower-stage penalty is zero at \(W=2\) and exceeds \(6.999\%\) relative to \(R_3^{II}\) at \(W=3\) under independent whole-plot assignment, while the centered HT benchmark is exactly blind to lower-stage balance.
gap: Bounded-outcome minimax theory is sharp for an unlayered randomized experiment, while split-plot theory supplies linear variance and limit results. There is no sharp unrestricted-risk theory for fixed counts imposed at two nested randomization layers.
fill: The project defines the hierarchical symmetry and endpoint extension explicitly, names a canonical orbit-game rule sequence and derives matching Airy upper and lower bounds for independent \(A\), gives an exact \(W=3\) fixed-lower saddle on every endpoint observation orbit and a certified independent-layer upper rule, and makes the missing matching three-plot and \(W=4,5,6\) certificates explicit gates for the fixed-upper-layer mixed interaction.
